thought.text: All three dev users can log in with the correct roles (alice has `activatedUser`, marie does not — as per the docs). Next, I'll verify the authenticated tRPC flow, database, and configuration files.

reasoning_content:
All three development users can log in successfully:
- alice: roles ['activatedUser', 'user']
- marie: roles ['default-roles-startuphafen', 'user']
- admin: works via admin-cli

This matches the documented behavior: alice is an activated standard user, marie is a new user without activation (no activatedUser role).

Next, I'll verify the following:
1. Whether the backend tRPC is working end-to-end (authenticated calls)
2. The database state
3. Whether the .localConfigs.json file exists and is gitignored
4. Whether Keycloak realm imports succeeded (users exist, theme exists)
5. Whether the maildev SMTP port is working

Also, let's test a tRPC endpoint that requires login (one with a Bearer token) and verify the full flow: frontend → caddy → tRPC backend → DB, plus authentication via Keycloak.

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "TOKEN=$(curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:28080/realms/startuphafen/protocol/openid-connect/token -d \"grant_type=password&client_id=startuphafen_app&username=alice&password=alice\" | python3 -c \"import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token'])\"); echo \"=== authenticated tRPC call via caddy :4000 ===\"; curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" http://localhost:4000/trpc/FeatureFlags.getFeatureFlags -w \"\\nHTTP %{http_code}\\n\" | head -5; echo \"=== trpc root (expect 404/NOT_FOUND without auth, as in logs) ===\"; curl -sS -o /dev/null -w \"HTTP %{http_code}\\n\" http://localhost:4000/trpc/", "summary": "Test authenticated tRPC via caddy"}
